failures.title: Aston Martin AJ133HP Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Supercharger Coupler Wear - 2013-2018
items.whatHappens: The Eaton supercharger on the AJ133HP uses a rubber isolation coupler to connect the supercharger rotors to the drive pulley. Over time, this coupler degrades and develops play, manifesting as a distinct metallic rattling or "marbles in a tin can" noise on deceleration or idle.
items.repairVsReplace: The coupler itself is a relatively inexpensive part (£150-£300), but accessing it requires partial removal of the supercharger assembly, making the labour cost significant (£800-£1,500). If ignored, the coupler can shred entirely, leading to a loss of boost and potential internal supercharger damage.

items.title: Coolant Crossover Pipe Leaks - 2013-2018
items.whatHappens: The AJ133 family utilises plastic coolant crossover pipes situated in the valley of the V8. Under extreme thermal cycling, these plastic fittings become brittle and develop micro-fractures, leading to coolant loss. In a high-performance application like the Rapide S, unchecked coolant loss can rapidly lead to overheating and catastrophic internal engine damage.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the crossover pipes with updated revisions is a standard preventative repair (£600-£1,200). However, if coolant loss has been ignored and the AJ133HP has overheated, a full engine replacement is the only viable path. Read our full coolant system failure guide.

items.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - 2013-2018
items.whatHappens: Early AJ133 variants (pre-2013) were notorious for timing chain tensioner failures. While the AJ133HP in the Rapide S benefits from revised, more robust tensioner designs, high-mileage examples can still experience chain stretch or guide wear, leading to a cold-start rattle.
items.repairVsReplace: A chain and tensioner replacement is a major service (£2,500-£4,500) due to the front-cover access requirements. If the chain has snapped, a full AJ133HP engine replacement is mandatory. Read our full timing chain failure guide.

failures.goodYearsLine: The AJ133HP benefits from the post-2013 revisions to the AJ133 family, making it significantly more robust than the early Vantage/XK iterations. However, strict adherence to annual coolant system inspections and supercharger noise monitoring remains critical for longevity .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the AJ133HP
variants.intro: The AJ133HP is the specific 558 PS high-output variant of the Aston Martin AJ133 5.0L V8 supercharged family. It is commonly confused with the standard AJ133 (510 PS, found in the DB9 and Vantage) or the AJ133S (575 PS, found in the Vantage S). You can confirm your exact engine code by checking the manufacturer plaque under the bonnet, consulting the vehicle's Aston Martin Heritage Certification or VIN decoder, or reading the alphanumeric stamping directly on the engine block. Fitting the wrong revision matters critically: while the physical block architecture is identical across the AJ133 family, the ECU mapping, supercharger pulley ratios, and specific ancillary mounting points differ between the standard, S, and HP variants. Installing a standard AJ133 unit without the bespoke Rapide S wiring loom, ECU, and supercharger calibration will result in persistent fault codes, severe performance loss, and potential drivetrain mismatch.

relatives.description: the AJ133HP was developed as a bespoke high-output variant for the Rapide S and has no direct predecessor within the Aston Martin lineup.

The 575 PS high-output variant found in the Vantage S; it shares the AJ133HP's performance orientation but features different calibration and physical mounting configurations, making it incompatible with the Rapide S without significant modification.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement AJ133HP - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used AJ133HP engine for sale can be a viable option only if it comes with a complete, stamped Aston Martin service history proving the supercharger coupler and coolant crossover pipes have been proactively replaced, and the dry-sump system health is verified. Given the extreme cost of supercharger or heat-related failure, buying used carries a premium risk. Browse vetted used AJ133HP engine options.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the recommended choice for the AJ133HP. A proper reconditioning process by an Aston Martin-certified specialist will replace the supercharger isolation coupler, all plastic coolant fittings, timing chain tensioners, and engine seals as standard, while also ensuring the specific Rapide S calibration is fully restored. This addresses the AJ133HP's core thermal and supercharger weaknesses in one go. Compare reconditioned AJ133HP options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is highly justified given the Rapide S's high asset value. A quality rebuild will include line-boring, new bearings, upgraded supercharger components, and a full diagnostic recalibration to factory specifications, often with the option to address known weak points with upgraded aftermarket parts. Explore rebuilt AJ133HP services.

faq.title: Aston Martin AJ133HP - Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: How much does an Aston Martin AJ133HP engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Aston Martin AJ133HP engine typically costs between £8,000 and £12,000 for supply only, or £9,680 to £14,240 fully fitted by a certified Aston Martin specialist. Used units start around £5,000 but carry a high risk of inherited supercharger or cooling system faults. Rebuilt units range from £12,000 to £18,000 for a comprehensive strip, rebuild, and supercharger refresh. Labour typically takes 14-18 hours due to the complex supercharger assembly and dry-sump oil system.

items.question: What is the most common problem with the AJ133HP engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues involve the supercharger isolation coupler wear and plastic coolant crossover pipe leaks. The supercharger coupler degrades over time, manifesting as a metallic rattling noise on deceleration or idle. The plastic coolant crossover pipes in the V8 valley become brittle under thermal cycling, leading to coolant loss and potential overheating. If coolant loss is ignored, it can rapidly lead to catastrophic internal engine damage in this high-performance application.

items.question: Which Aston Martin models use the AJ133HP engine?
items.answer: The Aston Martin AJ133HP was developed exclusively for the Rapide S (Series II), entering production in 2013 and continuing until production ended in 2018. It produces 410 kW (558 PS) and 620 Nm of torque. It serves as the sole powertrain option for this specific grand touring chassis.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned AJ133HP engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned AJ133HP is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the extreme complexity and cost of the supercharger and cooling system components. A proper reconditioning process by a certified specialist will replace the supercharger isolation coupler, all plastic coolant fittings, timing chain tensioners, and engine seals as standard. Used units rarely come with stamped proof that these expensive preventative updates have been completed, making them a high-risk investment.

Fitting a non-HP variant without the bespoke Rapide S wiring loom, ECU, and supercharger calibration will result in persistent fault codes and severe performance loss.
